article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 85% Indica / 15% Sativa
Genetics: Lavender × L.A. Confidential
Breeder: Soma’s Sacred Seeds
THC Content: 19–22%
CBD Content: Low / not officially specified by the breeder
Terpene Profile: caryophyllene , myrcene , linalool
Primary Flavors: Spicy hash, lavender, earthy Kush, citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late October
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Moderate
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Somalicious belongs to an older school of cannabis breeding in which flavor, resin quality, plant structure, and the character of the finished hash mattered just as much as headline cannabinoid percentages. Developed by Soma Seeds, this heavily indica-leaning marijuana variety brings together Lavender and L.A. Confidential genetics to create dense, resinous flowers with an unmistakably spicy, hash-oriented personality.

Soma’s own description emphasizes hard nuggets, purple coloration late in bloom, and particularly good performance when the flowers are processed into water hash . Rather than chasing the candy-dominant terpene profiles common in many contemporary hybrids, the plant leans into lavender, Afghani-style hash, Kush spice, citrus peel, and aromatic wood. The result is weed with a distinctly traditional character: rich, fragrant, physically relaxing, and built around the type of resin production that immediately attracts concentrate enthusiasts.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder identifies Somalicious primarily as a cross of Lavender and L.A. Confidential, producing an approximately 85% indica and 15% sativa hybrid. Soma Seeds’ listing also displays the notation “ Haze x Lavender / L.A. Confidential,” although the breeder’s detailed description explicitly states that the cultivar derives from L.A. Confidential crossed with Lavender. For practical lineage purposes, Lavender × L.A. Confidential is therefore the clearest breeder-supported parentage. The combination makes sense when examining the finished plant: Lavender contributes dark coloration, aromatic spice, and a complex old-school genetic background, while L.A. Confidential reinforces the compact growth, Kush influence, resin density, and deeply calming character.

Lavender itself is one of Soma’s better-known creations. The breeder lists its ancestry as Super Skunk × Big Skunk Korean × Afghani × Hawaiian and describes it as an 80% indica cultivar capable of developing exceptionally dark purple foliage and dense flowers carrying a spicy Afghani-hash scent. Those traits remain easy to recognize in Somalicious, particularly during the final portion of flowering when purple pigmentation can become pronounced. L.A. Confidential adds another strong indica component, helping explain why the completed hybrid remains compact despite Lavender’s ability to stretch when given a long vegetative period. Collectively, the genealogy gives this cannabis variety a broader heritage than its simple two-parent cross initially suggests, incorporating Afghani, Skunk, Hawaiian, Korean, and Kush-related influences.
Effects and Experience

The experience generally develops more gradually than the abrupt cerebral rush associated with strongly sativa-dominant marijuana. Early effects can feel warm, mentally settled, and mildly uplifting, with enough clarity remaining for conversation, music, or quiet creative activity. Soma describes the effect as powerful, soothing, long-lasting, and suitable for unwinding either alone or socially. That combination is important because the strain is not necessarily defined by immediate sedation. At moderate amounts, there can be a comfortable period in which the mind feels less hurried while awareness remains reasonably intact.

As the session progresses, the indica side tends to become more obvious. Physical tension may loosen, activity can become less appealing, and the overall mood shifts toward stillness. Higher doses are more likely to produce heaviness, drowsiness, or the desire to remain seated, especially for consumers with limited THC tolerance. Published potency estimates outside the breeder’s own material often place Somalicious around the upper-teens to low-20% THC range, but cannabinoid concentration should never be treated as a permanent property of a cultivar. Individual plants, harvest conditions, curing, and laboratory methodology can all change the measured result. For that reason, anyone unfamiliar with a particular batch should judge the flower by its tested label rather than assuming every example will have identical strength.
Medical Benefits

Somalicious is sometimes selected by medical cannabis consumers who prefer relaxing cultivars for evening symptom management. Its combination of mental decompression and bodily heaviness may be appealing to people dealing with temporary stress, difficulty settling down, muscle tension, or discomfort that interferes with rest. The later stages of the effect may also be useful for consumers who find stimulating marijuana counterproductive near bedtime. These applications should be understood as experience-based uses rather than clinical evidence that Somalicious specifically treats a disease.

The distinction matters because medical cannabis research generally evaluates cannabinoids, standardized preparations, or broader categories of cannabis use rather than individual commercial strain names. A cultivar’s terpene composition and THC concentration can also differ considerably between growers. Someone using weed for persistent pain, anxiety, insomnia, or another health concern should therefore treat strain descriptions as practical guidance rather than medical diagnosis or guaranteed treatment. High-THC cannabis may worsen anxiety, dizziness, impaired coordination, or rapid heartbeat in some individuals, so dose and personal tolerance remain more important than the reputation attached to the strain name.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Breaking apart a properly cured flower reveals the part of Somalicious that most clearly separates it from sweeter modern hybrids. The first aromatic layer tends toward dry spice, earthy Kush, and dark hashish rather than syrupy fruit. Lavender-like floral notes appear behind that foundation, while citrus zest and aromatic wood can brighten an otherwise dense profile. Soma Seeds specifically describes lavender, citrus fruit, and exotic woods in the aroma while also emphasizing the strain’s spicy taste and Kush-Afghani-hash smell.

Caryophyllene is frequently associated with peppery and woody cannabis aromas, while myrcene can contribute earthy, herbal depth and linalool is closely associated with floral lavender-like notes. These compounds fit the sensory description of the strain, although Somalicious should not be assumed to possess one universal terpene ratio without batch-specific laboratory testing. On inhalation, the flavor can seem sharper than the raw aroma suggests: spice and hash arrive first, followed by floral earthiness and a faint citrus edge. The finish is persistent, resinous, and distinctly old-school, making the cultivar particularly attractive to people who enjoy Kush, Afghan, and traditional hash flavors.
Growing Information

Somalicious grows with a sturdy, fairly compact framework, short internodal spacing, broad leaves, and enough lateral branching to form a small Christmas-tree-like silhouette. Soma characterizes it as a short-to-medium plant that develops large, bulky flowers beneath a heavy coating of resin. Indoor flowering generally requires about nine to ten weeks. Because the buds can become hard and dense, maintaining airflow through the canopy is important as flowering advances. Removing weak interior shoots and preventing excessive humidity around packed flower clusters can help reduce the conditions that encourage mold.

Purple coloration often becomes stronger near maturity, giving finished plants considerable visual appeal without requiring growers to manipulate temperatures excessively. Outdoors, Soma recommends warm, dry conditions or the protection of a greenhouse and places harvest near the end of October. That relatively late finish means cultivators in wet autumn climates need to pay particular attention to prolonged rain and nighttime humidity. Nutrient demands appear manageable, and the breeder describes the variety as hardy and relatively easy to cultivate, making it approachable for growers who already understand basic photoperiod cannabis care.

Resin production may be its most interesting cultivation characteristic. Mature flowers develop a substantial trichome layer, and Soma repeatedly highlights Somalicious as suitable for producing water hash. Growers interested in solventless processing may therefore value mature resin quality as much as raw flower weight. Allowing the trichomes to reach the desired maturity before harvest, drying gently, and avoiding excessive handling can help preserve the aromatic compounds and resin heads that give this cultivar much of its appeal.
FAQ
Is Somalicious an indica or sativa?

Somalicious is an indica-dominant hybrid. Soma Seeds lists the genetic balance at approximately 85% indica and 15% sativa. Its compact plant structure, broad foliage, dense flowers, and progressively relaxing effects are consistent with that strong indica influence.
What are the genetics of Somalicious?

The breeder describes the strain as a cross between Lavender and L.A. Confidential. Soma’s published product heading also references Haze, but the detailed breeder description repeatedly identifies Lavender × L.A. Confidential as the direct cross. Lavender itself contains Super Skunk, Big Skunk Korean, Afghani, and Hawaiian ancestry.
What does Somalicious taste like?

Expect a predominantly spicy, earthy, hash-forward profile. Lavender flowers, Kush, Afghani-style hash, citrus peel, and dry exotic wood can all appear in the aroma and flavor. It is considerably less dessert-like than many newer cannabis hybrids.
How long does Somalicious take to flower?

Indoor plants generally require approximately nine to ten weeks of flowering. Outdoors, the breeder places maturity around the end of October, making climate and late-season moisture important considerations.
Is Somalicious good for making hash?

Yes. Heavy resin coverage is one of its defining breeding traits, and Soma Seeds specifically recommends the cultivar for water-hash production. Dense trichome production, combined with its spicy Kush and lavender aromatics, makes the strain especially interesting for solventless concentrate enthusiasts.
Final Thoughts on Somalicious

Somalicious represents a style of cannabis breeding centered on resin, traditional indica character, and layered aroma rather than novelty flavor alone. Lavender supplies floral spice and dramatic purple expression, while L.A. Confidential anchors the cross with compact growth, Kush depth, and a heavier physical finish. The pairing produces weed that can remain socially comfortable at moderate amounts before moving toward a deeper, more restful state as the effects accumulate.

For growers, the attraction extends beyond the smoke itself. A manageable stature, substantial branching, dense trichome-coated buds, nine-to-ten-week flowering cycle, and proven suitability for water hash give the plant several practical advantages. For consumers, the combination of lavender, citrus, exotic wood, earth, spice, and Afghani-style hash provides an aromatic experience increasingly different from today’s fruit-and-candy-heavy market. Somalicious is consequently best viewed as a resin-focused, indica-dominant connoisseur cultivar with enough personality in both the garden and the jar to remain relevant well beyond the era in which its parent genetics first became famous.
